_note: How WAISentry controls and evidence map to common frameworks, for the fictional client Kitewing Software. Synthetic; not legal advice.
disclaimer: WAISentry supplies monitoring, response and evidence; it does not make an organisation compliant on its own. Final answers belong to the client and its broker, auditor or assessor.

questionnaire_bank.answer: Yes. Wursta WAISentry provides 24/7/365 monitoring: Gemini triage of all connected telemetry plus certified Wursta analysts who verify every real threat.

Yes. Four containment playbooks are pre-approved (session termination, OAuth app revocation, targeted account suspension, Drive quarantine); after analyst confirmation they complete in under 60 seconds. Other actions are escalated to Kitewing's on-call.

Partially. EDR is healthy on 56 of 58 EDR-capable endpoints and all 3 servers; ChromeOS devices rely on verified boot and DNS filtering. Gaps: one contractor BYOD laptop (EDR being installed) and a retired reception PC.
Yes. 2-step verification is enforced for all 62 people and all admins; 60 use hardware security keys and 2 contractors use Google prompts until their keys arrive on 2026-11-09.
Scored security events are retained for 400 days and raw logs for 90 days, inside Kitewing's own Google Cloud tenant.
Yes. Mimecast filters inbound mail with impersonation and URL protection, DMARC is at p=quarantine, and WAISentry correlates mail alerts with identity signals.
Yes. KnowBe4 training and monthly simulations; phish-prone percentage fell from 21.0% to 9.7%; 58 of 62 completed this year's training.
Bank-detail changes are verified by phone using the number on file (client finance procedure). WAISentry detects payment-diversion attempts; one was stopped on 2026-11-01 with no loss.
Not covered by WAISentry — Kitewing IT to answer from its backup records.

One legacy server remains (Windows Server 2016 file server, support ends 2027-01-12, replacement planned); the out-of-support reception PC was removed on 2026-10-31. Laptop patch status is monitored daily.
Yes. Since 2026-11-03 unverified third-party apps cannot be granted access; 14 apps are allowlisted and WAISentry reviews OAuth grants and shadow IT continuously. 4 legacy grants are being revoked.

Yes — security incidents occurred and were contained with no financial loss and no confirmed data breach; the most significant was an attempted payment diversion on 2026-11-01 ($48,600 at risk, $0 lost). Details in the case file.
Yes. Kitewing's incident-response plan is tested annually; WAISentry playbooks and the escalation matrix are part of it, and a live incident on 2026-11-01 exercised it end to end.
Security telemetry is evaluated inside Kitewing's own Google Cloud tenant; names, emails, file names and message content are tokenised before any alert reaches the SOC.
